doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Respecting and paying musicians
summary: Hampton insists musicians be paid early and given rest before concerts.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: The beginning of the recording was, but not the other idea, because I’m the only person that believes, when musicians play, that they should be respected. They should be paid as much as you can pay them. They should be given conditions that puts them in a situation where they’re able to feel best about their performance. They shouldn’t necessarily have to wait until the last minute to get their money. If they come in, and they’re going to play the concert, pay them, so they don’t feel like they’ve got to wait after and try to tackle you to get your money and stuff like that. This is the way that I want it to go. I want it to go that the musicians are given the utmost of respect. They’re given the best situation to play in. We’re going to do everything that makes it possible for them to have the most energy to make this concert possible. They don’t have to play just before the concert or anything like that. We do all the rehearsals before, another day of the concert. We might do a little playing as far as sound check is concerned. I don’t want them to be . . .

. . . taxed with it, playing, eating dinner, and then playing the concert. I want them to have some time between all of that, so they can feel the very best. They can really get their teeth into this music.
